title: Sort Array By Parity
spaceBreakdown:
- No containers, arrays, or strings allocated
- No recursion
- Input vector modified in place; returned vector is the same object
approach: Use two pointers starting from opposite ends of the array. The left pointer advances past even numbers; the right pointer retreats past odd numbers. When the left pointer lands on an odd and the right on an even, swap them. This partitions the array in place so all evens precede all odds in a single pass, without needing extra space or a stable sort.
hints: If you only need two groups (even-first, odd-second) and don't care about order within each group, what single property of each number determines which half it belongs in?
Use two pointers, one at each end, moving inward. On `[3,1,2,4]`: left=0 sees odd 3, right=3 sees even 4 - swap them to get `[4,1,2,3]`, then advance both pointers inward.

**All odd** - every element is odd, so the right pointer must stop before going out of bounds
`Input: nums = [1,3,5,7]` → `Expected: [1,3,5,7]`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `left < right` guard in the inner while that decrements `right` → right drops to -1 and evaluates `nums[-1]`, causing undefined behavior

**Already partitioned** - evens already precede odds, so no swaps should occur
`Input: nums = [2,4,1,3]` → `Expected: [2,4,1,3]`
⚠️ Bug: swapping without re-checking `left < right` after the inner whiles → swaps `nums[2]` and `nums[1]`, returning `[2,1,4,3]`

**Single element** - n = 1, the boundary index must be valid
`Input: nums = [0]` → `Expected: [0]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `right = nums.size()` instead of `nums.size() - 1` → accesses `nums[1]` on a one-element array, out of bounds

**All even** - every element is even, so the left pointer must stop before going out of bounds
`Input: nums = [2,4,6,8]` → `Expected: [2,4,6,8]`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `left < right` guard in the inner while that increments `left` → left reaches 4 and evaluates `nums[4]`, out of bounds

followUps.q: What if the relative order of even elements among themselves and odd elements among themselves must be preserved (stable partition)?
followUps.a: Iterate once collecting evens in order, then iterate again collecting odds in order, writing both into a new array. TC: O(n), SC: O(n). The in-place two-pointer swap approach is not stable because it reorders elements within each group.

followUps.q: What if the input is a stream too large to fit in memory and you must output evens-first in batches?
followUps.a: Make two passes over the stream: first emit every even element, then re-read the stream and emit every odd element. TC: O(n), SC: O(1) auxiliary. If only one pass is allowed, buffer the odds in a bounded queue and flush evens immediately, then drain the queue at the end - SC: O(k) where k is the number of odds buffered.

followUps.q: What if you must partition into three groups (e.g., multiples of 3, then even non-multiples of 3, then the rest) in one pass?
followUps.a: Apply the Dutch national flag algorithm with three pointers (low, mid, high). Classify each element by its category and swap it into the correct zone, advancing the appropriate pointer. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).
